title: Each change is gated in a fresh container
what: The gate of each change also runs in a fresh container with the tools preinstalled and only the project's files; the two results are compared per wave; after 3 waves in a row agree, the container's result decides; the container never lands anything.
why: Owner, 26-27 Oct: "...вплоть до того что бы можем запускать каждое изменение в новой docker контейнере где предустановлены все необходимые утилиты, как будто это запуск ci/cd в стандартных системах (woodpecker)... При этом получать тот же результат". Owner's answers, 27 Oct: "3. A" (this Mac re-gates until 3 waves in a row agree with the container, then the container's gate decides), "4. A" (containers after the metrics build). Measured 27 Oct: container start 0.33-0.52 s cached, image 1.18 GB, cold build 311 s; same tree b10d314 quick gate green on the Mac in 935 s and red in a Linux container (25 failures, 17 errors, 215 s; queued as the-quick-gate-is-red-in-a-clean-linux-container). Needs the same-setup item first (a-change-runs-with-relay-s-settings-from-the-pro). Design source: scratchpad report design-clean-env.md rev 2 (approach A, never landing from the container); redo against the fresh repository when taken. IP 84 chosen by the front from the owner's "4. A" (agent-chosen).
where: a container image definition in the repo

fact: Migration 27 Oct: the link in `why` line 1 points to a session file (`design-clean-env.md` revision 2 of 27 Oct, in the session session folder; a copy is in relay's backup folder on the owner's Mac), which is deleted when the machine restarts; the facts it held that this item rests on are the notes below.

Design 27 Oct (clean-environment design, revision 2, section 8): do B first, then A. B = relay becomes project-local on the host (plugins, rules and settings come from the project's own repository); A = a container per change. B is the precondition of A: A without B is either a container with no plugins, rules or memory, or a container with the host's ~/.claude copied in, which is global settings in a box.

Measured 27 Oct: a container starts in 0.33-0.52 s cached and a clone takes 1.51 s, against a 215-935 s gate; the quick gate on one tree was green on the host and gave 25 failures and 17 errors in a container; two causes are relay defects: `ps` missing (18 errors) and `sum([0.1]*100)`, which is 10.0 on Python 3.14 and 9.99999999999998 on 3.11.

Measured 27 Oct: what a change depends on differs on 8 of 10 lines of the global-state table (plugins switched on, marketplace path, model and effort, permissions, rules text, memory, old agents and hooks, ledger, gate slots, test times); a fresh container without the plugins runs no hooks and no typed agents, so merges go unguarded and nothing is recorded.

Decided in that design (the owner can reverse each): the front and the landing stay on the host; containers run build, gate, review, fix and check but never land, take the default branch or build a train; no `--bare`; the rule files and the run's settings are generated per run and never committed; one exact Python 3.14.6 for the gate on the host and in the image; no paid runs in a container (RELAY_PAID=off). Not verified: that the Workflow tool and the InstructionsLoaded hook work under `claude -p`; that a directory marketplace accepts a relative path in project settings.

29 Oct, measured while designing the Linux fence: the quick gate in a Linux container (repository cloned inside, not mounted) took 1.1 to 2.5 min over 6 runs (all red: 30 failures, 22 errors of 1,788 tests), against 4.4 and 11.8 min for the Mac quick gate without the second run (1 run each, different loads). Container start 0.21-0.29 s plus clone 2.3-2.4 s. Through podman's shared folder git is 30-90 times slower than native, so the repository must be cloned in; with it cloned, podman and Docker ran the tests in about the same time.
